messages.content:
You are the Policy & Legal Adviser Agent in a health-data safety prototype set in the UAE. You answer what published rules say about a situation, using ONLY the search_policy tool.
Rules:
- Search before answering, as many times as needed. Run separate targeted searches for each point, using different wording, and search each relevant jurisdiction (UAE federal, Dubai, Abu Dhabi). Passages are returned in full: read all of each one, since a provision may sit anywhere in it. Do not rely on memory.
- Cite ONLY chunk_ids returned by your searches. Quote or paraphrase only what the passage says.
- Report conflicts between provisions, unclear jurisdictional scope, and ambiguities. If you cannot find a provision on a point, say so as a gap of type no_provision_found. That means not found in this knowledge base, which is not proof that no rule exists.
- Give no legal conclusions or advice. State what the texts say and where they leave a question open.
- Use EU or ITU passages only as clearly labelled comparisons.
When finished, reply with ONLY JSON of this shape:
{"requirements":[{"statement":str,"citations":[chunk_id]}],"conflicts":[{"description":str,"citations":[chunk_id]}],"gaps":[{"title":str,"type":"conflict|scope_unclear|no_provision_found|ambiguity","description":str,"citations":[chunk_id],"recommendation":str}],"comparisons":[{"statement":str,"citations":[chunk_id]}],"caveats":[str]}

Situation:
Event 5 (2026-11-08T02:30): Emergency: clinician at Hospital A requests Hospital B's medication list
Fatima arrives unconscious at Hospital A with bleeding. The doctor needs her full medication list, including Hospital B's, and requests break-the-glass access. She has opted out of NABIDH.

Institutions: HospitalA = Hospital A (synthetic, cardiology), Abu Dhabi, exchange Malaffi; HospitalB = Hospital B (synthetic, nephrology), Dubai, exchange NABIDH; HospitalC = Hospital C (synthetic, endocrinology), Abu Dhabi, exchange Malaffi
Consent module decisions:
- ED_btg_B_meds: denied [EMERGENCY_BLOCKED_BY_OPT_OUT] Emergency access was not granted because the patient opted out of NABIDH. A human decision is required. Basis: DHA/HISHD/ST-09 (Standards for Health Information Consent and Access Control, 2025) section 9.7: PHI of an opted-out patient should not be retrieved using BTG access (escalated to a human)
Safety engine findings now: DEMO-LAB-001:glucophage (high)
Limitation: HospitalB: data withheld from assessment by the patient's choice (since 2026-11-07). The safety assessment is incomplete.

Question: A clinician at an Abu Dhabi hospital requests emergency access to this patient's records held by a Dubai hospital. The patient has revoked the sharing grants and opted out of the Dubai exchange. What do the rules say about emergency access here, and are there conflicts or unclear points?

Entity should implement session time-out controls to prevent unauthorized access. 16.10. Processes should be implemented to monitor all HIS access and use. This includes regular audits of user access to ensure that access is pertinent to the user`s role and use of the system and related information is in line with the conditions under which access was granted. 16.11. The Account Management standard operating procedure (SOP) must be completed for each HIS and reviewed regularly (at least annually). 16.12. All consents must be archived along with medical records as per DHA regulations. 16.13. Accessing to consent and sharing them with Data Subjects/Patients and/or DHA inspectors (for auditing purposes) should be obtainable. 17. STANDARD THIRTEEN: BREAK THE GLASS ACCESS 17.1. Only physicians who provide direct care to the Data Subject/Patient must be allowed to access to HIS through Break the Glass (BTG)."}, {"chunk_id": "dha-consent-access-standard-2025#0004", "citation": "Standards for Health Information Consent and Access Control, Version 1 (2025), p.7 [dha-consent-access-standard-2025#0004]", "scope": "Dubai", "text": "Authentication: The process of reliable security identification of subjects by incorporating an identifier and its authenticator. Authorization: The granting of rights, which includes the granting of access based on access rights. Breach: Any unauthorized access, disclosure, acquisition or use of Subject of care Data, whether by willful misconduct or otherwise or any breach of DHA Policies. A Breach is a Reportable Event that, once investigated, is confirmed to have compromise the security or privacy of the Personal Health Information (PHI). Break The Glass: Allows health professionals to gain access to protected health information (PHI) in the health information system (HIS), without the Patient's consent, when necessary to lessen or prevent a serious threat to a Patient’s health such as emergency situations. Confidentiality: Part of the information security triad, confidentiality means the property that information is not made available or disclosed to unauthorized individuals, entities, or processes. Standards for Health Information Consent and Access Control Code: DHA/HISHD/ST-09 Issue Nu: 1 Issue Date: 02/01/2025 Effective Date: 02/04/2025 Revision Date: 02/01/2030        Page 8 of 42 Consent: Is the fact that permission has been given. A person who consents to something is, in effect, giving permission for that thing to happen. Data: Set of information, facts, concepts, instruction s, observations, or measurements in the form of numbers, letters, words, symbols, images, videos, signs, sounds, maps, or any other form, generated, processed, stored, interpreted, or exchanged, by individuals or Information and Communications Technology (ICT)."}, {"chunk_id": "dha-consent-access-standard-2025#0019", "citation": "Standards for Health Information Consent and Access Control, Version 1 (2025), p.23 [dha-consent-access-standard-2025#0019]", "scope": "Dubai", "text": "9.9.2. The Data Subject/Patient sings the consent and send it to DHA Nabidh team. 9.9.3. DHA Nabidh team will opt out the Data Subject/Patient from Nabidh as p er request. 10. STANDARD SIX: GRANTING ACCESS TO HEALTH INFORMATION SYSTEMS 10.1. To the extent, technologically feasible users should be granted access only to health information required to perform their appropriate functions at the Entity. Standards for Health Information Consent and Access Control Code: DHA/HISHD/ST-09 Issue Nu: 1 Issue Date: 02/01/2025 Effective Date: 02/04/2025 Revision Date: 02/01/2030        Page 24 of 42 10.2. Access must be restricted to specific functions within some applications; and whenever the software allows, access should be as granular as feasible. 10.3. Each user in the Entity should sign a “User and Confidentiality Access Agreement” before accessing PHI through HIS. 10.4. Entity must issue passwords and Unique User Identification (“ID”) for accessing Entity’s HIS once the “User and Confidentiality Access Agreement” is completed and submitted. Such passwords and IDs should not be shared with any other individuals or Entities. 10.5. In configuring access, all Entities must follow the concept of “need to know” and ‘least privilege’: Access should be granted on need-to-know basis and least privileges.  Every HIS and every user of the system should operate using the least set of privilege s necessary to complete their job. This principle limits the damage that can result from data breach."}]

{"requirements":[{"statement":"According to the DHA Standards for Health Information Consent and Access Control (DHA/HISHD/ST-09), if a patient has opted out of the Health Information System (HIS), their Personal Health Information (PHI) should not be retrieved using Break-the-Glass (BTG) access.","citations":["dha-consent-access-standard-2025#0018"]}],"conflicts":[],"gaps":[{"title":"Emergency access for opted-out patients","type":"no_provision_found","description":"While the standards explicitly prohibit the use of BTG access for patients who have opted out of the HIS, there is no provision in the provided text detailing alternative procedures for clinicians to obtain life-saving information in emergency situations when the patient has opted out.","citations":["dha-consent-access-standard-2025#0018"],"recommendation":"Consult institutional emergency protocols or DHA guidance for procedures regarding emergency access when automated systems are blocked by patient opt-out."}],"comparisons":[],"caveats":["The provided rules are specific to the Dubai Health Authority (DHA) Standards for Health Information Consent and Access Control (DHA/HISHD/ST-09). The applicability of these specific provisions to cross-emirate data exchange (e.g., between Malaffi in Abu Dhabi and NABIDH in Dubai) is not explicitly detailed in the provided text."]}

You have run only 1 search(es). Before answering, run further targeted searches with different wording, covering each relevant jurisdiction (UAE federal, Dubai, Abu Dhabi). Do not conclude that a provision is missing until you have searched for it from several angles.
